To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the X-ray selected AGN sample has a high percentage of obscured objects (26%) and this fraction is in disagreement with current XRB synthesis model predictions.

the fraction of XRB absorbed AGNs is over predicted by current XRB synthesis model and the AGN unification scheme is supported by the correlation between X-ray absorption properties and optical spectral type.
the fraction of absorbed X-ray AGNs is significantly larger than that predicted by current models of the XRB, and that this fraction is not constant with flux.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the obscuration in the hard X-ray band (4.6-7.5keV), using a sample of X-ray sources selected from the XMM-Newton Hard Bright Survey.
the study of the obscuration properties in a sample of hard X-ray selected sources.
the analysis of a complete sample of X-ray selected AGN, which is the first to be selected in the energy band 4.5 to 7.5 kev.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the XRB synthesis models overestimate the number of absorbed AGNs in the hard X-ray band, but this is not the case in the soft X-ray band.
X-ray selected hard X-ray AGNs (4.5 keV-10 keV) are not a good proxy for the population of X-ray selected soft X-ray AGNs.
the AGN unification model is a good description of the X-ray selected AGN population, but that there are still problems in reproducing the observed XRB.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the X-ray selected sample is dominated by unobscured type 1 AGN, with the fraction of obscured AGN increasing with decreasing flux, and that the XRB synthesis models overpredict the fraction of obscured sources at the fluxes probed in this survey.
the XRB synthesis models over predict the fraction (and number) of absorbed AGNs at all the flux limits considered.
the X-ray selected AGN population in the local Universe is not well understood and more work is necessary to understand the nature of these AGNs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the XMM-Newton Hard Bright Survey is the first sample of serendipitous sources selected in the hard band (4. 5-7. 5 keV) to have complete spectroscopy.
the X-ray selected hard band (4.0-7.0 keV) AGN population is dominated by obscured AGNs.
, in order to reproduce the X-ray background (XRB), current models over predict the fraction and/or luminosity density of obscured AGNs.
